title: US military identifies 2 soldiers killed during Iranian strikes in Jordan and 1 killed during drone detonation in Iraq | CNN Politics
text:
Source: CNN

The Department of Defense on Mondayidentified two US soldierswho were killed in Iranian strikes in Jordan, and on Tuesday identified another soldier believed to be killed in the Jordan attack and a service member killed in Iraq.

1st Lt. Tyler James Feehan, 25, and Pvt. Isabella Gonzales, 19, were killed as part of the Friday attack on Muwaffaq Salti Air Base in Jordan.

Sgt. Angel S. Rampersad, 28, is believed to have been killed in action during the same Friday attack in Jordan, according to the Pentagon. The soldier was previously listed as missing by US Central Command.

The department on Tuesday identified another service member who was killed in action during a controlled detonation of a downed Iranian drone in Iraq. Sgt. Michael Emmanuel Swinton of Fayetteville, North Carolina, was killed on July 19.

Gonzales, of Carrollton, Texas, died Friday, the Defense Department said.

Feehan, who enlisted in Ewa Beach, Hawaii, but whose father told CNN he primarily lived in Georgia, died Saturday.

Feehan’s parents told CNN they are “completely heartbroken and devastated,” adding that their son was set to be married when he returned from deployment.

“We want America and the world to know Tyler lived life to the fullest and accomplished more in his 25 years than most complete in a lifetime,” Stephen and Shari Feehan said.

Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claimed responsibility for the attacks in Jordan in a statement on Saturday. The Pentagon said the soldiers who died in Jordan were killed “during an enemy attack.” Other American service members suffered injuries, including four who had to be medically evacuated to a hospital in Jordan but have since been discharged, US Central Command said over the weekend.

The Pentagon said authorities would continue to investigate the attack.

The deaths, initially announced on Saturday, marked the first American casualties resulting from Iranian strikes since March.

Before the Pentagon identified Rampersad, it announced over the weekend that the US located unidentified remains of a missing service member in Jordan. The remains have yet to be conclusively identified, but the military believes it to be Rampersad.

A dignified transfer of the four service members will take place on Wednesday, according to an administration official.

The deaths bring the number of USservice memberswho have died in the nearly five-month war to 18, including the soldier believed to have been killed in Jordan.

Six US Army Reserve soldierswere killed March 1by a direct Iranian strike on a makeshift operations center at Kuwait’s Shuaiba port. Days later, an Army sergeantdied after sustaining injuriesduring an attack in Saudi Arabia.

On March 12,six service members were killedwhen a US Air Force KC-135 Stratotanker, a refueling aircraft, crashed in western Iraq, though the incident was “not due to hostile or friendly fire.”

A recent lull in fighting had given way to what hasmore resembled an all-out warover the past week, with the US targeting Iranian railways, roads and tunnels, while Iran has launched attacks against an expanding list of countries in the region.

Despite the attacks, officials held out hope for the possibility of a diplomatic solution over the weekend. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Sunday the US “remains open” to talks, while an official representing Iran said they were similarly open to discussions.

President Donald Trump said Saturday that the deaths of the American service members were “a very sad thing.”

“We hate to see it happen,” he toldNewsNation. “It’s in service to our country.”

CNN’s Francesca Hoffman contributed to this report.

This story has been updated with additional information.
